title: Ecommerce Ad Agency: How to Evaluate One
summary: Choose an ecommerce ad agency around product economics, creative and measurement. Compare catalog needs, video briefs, reporting access and total fees.
body_markdown:
## Which products should enter the first agency brief?


Choose products that the business can confidently support through the intended campaign period. Review availability, product information, fulfillment expectations and the offer with the relevant owners. A popular item is not automatically the best first brief if its assets are inaccurate or its advertised configuration cannot be purchased.


Create a product-readiness sheet. For each candidate, record the exact SKU, current price and offer, usable images or footage, supported selling points, destination and availability owner. Mark missing inputs instead of letting the agency improvise them. This helps the team identify a feasible starting point while longer-term product work continues.


For an illustrative bag store, one model may have current photography, an accurate size guide and dependable stock. Another may have a compelling feature but only outdated images. The first may be easier to brief responsibly. That is a production-readiness judgment, not a claim that it will generate a better advertising return.


Ask the agency how it would connect the selected product to a buyer situation. “Promote the bag” leaves the message open. “Show how the approved model organizes a workday's essentials using the actual compartments” creates a concrete requirement for the script and demonstration.


## How do you turn product objections into distinct ads?


Separate questions about identity, use and purchase conditions. A viewer may need to recognize the item, understand how it works or resolve an objection about buying it. Those questions can call for different creative even when every ad links to the same product.


For the bag example, a capacity demonstration could show the actual items that fit. A routine scene could show how someone carries it through a workday. A detail-focused ad could explain a verified material or compartment feature. Use only the facts and demonstrations the business can support. Do not change the apparent dimensions or storage capacity to make the scene more impressive.


Write each concept as a short chain: buyer question, message, proof and next action. Then identify possible variants within the concept. A different opening line for the capacity demonstration is a variant of that idea; a new gift-buying scenario is a different message. Keep the distinction in the production plan and quote.


Request an annotated first draft that shows where the proof appears. If a script promises organization but the edit contains only attractive lifestyle shots, the creative has not yet supplied the evidence the brief asked for. Correct the communication problem before polishing transitions or multiplying aspect-ratio exports.


## What should the team do when the offer or stock changes?


Create a change path that connects the commercial owner, campaign owner and production team. The person who learns about an offer change should know where to report it and which approved ads are affected. Keep the destination and creative in the same review rather than updating one and assuming the other remains accurate.


Imagine an illustrative promotion that changes from a bundle to a single-item offer. The campaign owner needs a decision about existing ads. The production team needs the replacement wording and any new end card. The product or store owner needs to confirm the destination. Those tasks can be coordinated by one agency, but each still requires an accountable owner.


Maintain a lightweight asset register with product, offer, destination, approval date and final filename. When a product changes, use the register to identify affected creative. Archive superseded versions so a buyer does not accidentally relaunch an outdated offer from a shared folder.


Agree how urgent corrections differ from new concepts in the service scope. This is a contract question, not a reason to invent a universal revision policy. Ask each supplier to explain its process and price the work you expect to need.


## How should an ecommerce campaign review connect back to production?


Review results alongside the product and offer context. Ask what changed during the observation period, which version actually ran and whether the destination remained accurate. If those basics are unclear, resolve them before concluding that the creative idea failed.


For example, a demonstration ad and a lifestyle ad might generate different patterns of engagement. The useful next step depends on the business outcome and the available evidence. You might need a clearer demonstration, stronger offer explanation or more time to observe the campaign. Record the reason for the next brief rather than copying whichever visual happened to appear beside the largest number.

That gives the business a clear place to assign the connection between product truth, creative production and campaign decisions.


Before renewing or expanding, inspect whether the operating process is working: accurate inputs, timely decisions, approved usable assets and an understandable review. Then decide what additional production or campaign work the evidence supports. This is more specific than asking for a larger monthly video count without identifying the questions those videos should answer.

## Key takeaways


- Put product economics and constraints in the brief.
- Give each asset a clear selling job.
- Preserve product truth across creative variants.
- Check the ad and its destination with the[message-match guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/ad-landing-page-message-match) .


## FAQ


### Should my agency also manage retention marketing?


Include it only when it is part of the need and written scope. Email, lifecycle messaging and repeat-purchase analysis require explicit ownership even if the same supplier also handles acquisition.


### Can AI generate all my product footage?


Do not assume it can represent every product interaction accurately. Identify shots requiring exact evidence and use real footage or approved assets when that is the appropriate way to prove the claim.


### How do I compare two ecommerce agency quotes?


Ask each supplier to price the same responsibilities, deliverables, rights and review process. Keep the media budget separate and show how fees change when spend or production volume increases.


### What should I provide for a first batch?


Provide current product assets, approved claims, the actual offer and destination, brand rules, stock constraints and one approval owner. Identify who can confirm product or availability changes. Add the business outcome and reporting source, then ask the agency to connect each proposed concept to a buyer question and supporting proof.
